style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: An alphabet of God's works -- twenty-two half-lines, one per Hebrew letter, the first of a matched pair with Psalm 112, which uses the same acrostic form to describe the man who fears the God this psalm describes. It begins with a Hallelujah and a whole heart in the assembly, and then it studies: the works of the LORD are great, searched out by everyone who delights in them. What follows is a catalogue: His work is majesty and splendor; His righteousness stands forever; He made His wonders memorable; He is gracious and compassionate; He feeds those who fear Him; He remembers His covenant forever; He showed His people His power by giving them the nations' land; His hands' work is truth and justice; His precepts are trustworthy and permanent; He sent redemption; He ordained His covenant forever; His name is holy and awesome. And then the line the whole wisdom tradition rests on -- the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom -- placed at the end of a psalm that has just shown what there is to fear and love. Study first, then wisdom; the acrostic is the syllabus.

1.text: Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart, in the council of the upright and in the congregation.
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD ['Hallelujah', halelu-Yah, the KJV margin]. I will praise [yadah] the LORD [YHWH] with my whole heart [lebab], in the assembly [sod -- the intimate council] of the upright [yashar], and in the congregation [edah].
1.notes: The acrostic begins after the halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050): odeh YHWH be-khol-lebab (H3034, H3824) -- with ALL the heart -- be-sod yesharim ve-edah (H5475, H3477, H5712): the sod is the intimate circle of Psalm 25:14, the edah the whole assembly. Thanksgiving in the small room and the big one.

2.text: Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who take delight in them.
2.amp: The works [maaseh] of the LORD [YHWH] are great [gadol], sought out [darash -- searched, studied] of all them that have pleasure [chephets -- delight] therein.
2.notes: gedolim maase YHWH (H1419, H4639): the works are great -- derushim le-khol-chephtsehem (H1875, H2656): darash is the study-verb, the root of midrash; the works are RESEARCHED by those who delight in them. The verse carved over the door of the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge: delight is the motive of all real inquiry.

3.text: His work is majesty and splendor, and His righteousness stands forever.
3.amp: His work [poal] is honourable [hod -- majesty] and glorious [hadar -- splendor]: and His righteousness [tsedaqah] endures [amad -- stands] for ever [ad].
3.notes: hod-ve-hadar poolo (H1935, H1926, H6467): majesty and splendor, the royal pair of Psalm 104:1, describing His WORK -- ve-tsidqato omedet la-ad (H6666, H5975, H5703): righteousness that stands -- the refrain Psalm 112 will apply to the righteous man (112:3, 9).

4.text: He has made His wonders something to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and full of compassion.
4.amp: He has made [asah] His wonderful works [pala -- wonders] to be remembered [zeker -- a memorial]: the LORD [YHWH] is gracious [channun] and full of compassion [rachum].
4.notes: zekher asah le-niphleotav (H2143, H6213, H6381): He built a MEMORIAL for His wonders -- the feasts, the Passover, the Sabbath, all designed to make forgetting difficult. channun ve-rachum YHWH (H2587, H7349): Exodus 34:6's pair, the reason the wonders happened.

5.text: He has provided food for those who fear Him; His covenant He keeps in mind forever.
5.amp: He has given [natan] meat ['prey', tereph -- food, provision, the KJV margin] unto them that fear [yare] Him: He will ever [olam] be mindful [zakar] of His covenant [berith].
5.notes: tereph natan li-reav (H2964, H5414, H3373): tereph is literally prey -- the food a lion tears -- so the provision is pictured as hunted and brought home for the God-fearers (manna, quail). yizkor le-olam berito (H2142, H5769, H1285): the memorial of verse 4 works both ways -- He remembers too.

6.text: He has displayed to His people the strength of His works, in handing them the nations' inheritance.
6.amp: He has showed [nagad -- declared] His people [am] the power [koach] of His works [maaseh], that He may give [natan] them the heritage [nachalah] of the heathen [goy].
6.notes: koach maasav higgid le-ammo (H3581, H4639, H5046, H5971): the power of His works DECLARED -- by the conquest: latet lahem nachalat goyim (H5414, H5159, H1471), giving them the nations' inheritance. Joshua's book as an exhibit of divine strength.

7.text: What His hands do is truth and justice; every one of His precepts can be trusted,
7.amp: The works [maaseh] of His hands [yad] are verity [emeth -- truth] and judgment [mishpat -- justice]; all His commandments [piqqudim -- precepts] are sure [aman -- trustworthy, firm].
7.notes: maase yadav emet u-mishpat (H4639, H3027, H571, H4941): what His hands make is truth and justice -- neemanim kol-piqqudav (H539, H6490): His precepts are made firm by aman, the root of 'amen'. The acrostic turns from works to words at its midpoint.

8.text: established forever and ever, carried out in truth and uprightness.
8.amp: They stand fast ['are established', samak -- upheld, the KJV margin] for ever [ad] and ever [olam], and are done [asah] in truth [emeth] and uprightness [yashar].
8.notes: semukhim la-ad le-olam (H5564, H5703, H5769): samak is the leaning-verb of Psalm 3:5 -- the precepts are propped up permanently, the double-forever of Psalm 145. asuyim be-emet ve-yashar (H6213, H571, H3477): done in truth and straightness -- His commands are as upright as His deeds.

9.text: He has sent His people redemption; His covenant He has commanded for all time. His name is holy and awesome.
9.amp: He sent [shalach] redemption [peduth -- ransom, deliverance] unto His people [am]: He has commanded [tsavah] His covenant [berith] for ever [olam]: holy [qadosh] and reverend [yare -- awesome, to be feared] is His name [shem].
9.notes: pedut shalach le-ammo (H6304, H7971, H5971): redemption SENT -- the exodus as a dispatch from heaven, and the Gospel as the second sending. tsivvah-le-olam berito (H6680, H5769, H1285): the covenant commanded, not negotiated. qadosh ve-nora shemo (H6918, H3372, H8034): holy and awesome -- 'reverend' in the KJV's sense, a title the Bible gives only to God's name.

10.text: The fear of the LORD is where wisdom begins; all who practice it gain good insight. His praise stands forever.
10.amp: The fear [yirah] of the LORD [YHWH] is the beginning [reshith -- the first thing, the chief part] of wisdom [chokmah]: a good ['good success', tov, the KJV margin] understanding [sekel -- insight] have all they that do [asah] His commandments ['them', the KJV margin]: His praise [tehillah] endures [amad -- stands] for ever [ad].
10.notes: reshit chokhmah yirat YHWH (H7225, H2451, H3374): the motto of Proverbs 1:7 and 9:10, placed here at the END of a psalm that has just laid out what there is to fear -- the acrostic is the syllabus, the fear is the graduation. sekhel tov le-khol-osehem (H7922, H2896, H6213): insight comes to the DOERS. tehillato omedet la-ad (H8416, H5975, H5703): the standing-verb of verse 3, now for His praise.
